question.text: Per the April 10, 2023 SEBI circular on distribution/placement commissions for AIFs, how may Category I and Category II AIFs pay the distribution fee to distributors?

answer.text: 100% upfront at the time of investor on-boarding.
Up to one-half upfront and the remaining as a single payment at exit.
Up to one-third of the total distribution fee / placement fee on upfront basis, and the remaining on equal trail basis over the tenure of the fund.
Only on trail basis over 10 years — no upfront permitted.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD/CIR/2023/054 dated April 10, 2023, Category I and II AIFs may pay UP TO ONE-THIRD of the total distribution/placement fee on upfront basis, with the remaining paid on EQUAL TRAIL BASIS over the tenure of the fund. (Cat III is treated differently — full trail.) The Trap: 100% upfront encourages churn-style misselling and is not permitted. One-half upfront is too high. 100% trail over 10 years is closer to Cat III rule, not Cat I/II. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A Distributor tests this for sell-side; XIX-D Manager tests it for pay-side compliance. XIX-B Cat III Distributor applies the full-trail Cat III rule — do not swap. Manager's Pro-Tip: When negotiating with a distributor, pre-compute the NPV of 1/3-upfront + 2/3-trail over expected fund tenure — distributors over-value the upfront; use trail-NPV to rationalise total placement cost.
